recipes.name: Sagano Smoke
observations: Menu lists Hibiki Harmony, Ardbeg Wee Beastie, matcha, honey, lemon, and whole egg.
Menu price: $24 at time of visit.
Photograph shows an opaque green cocktail served up in a stemmed glass with a thick pale-green foam cap and fine green powder dusting.
No ice visible in the serving glass.

ingredients.name: Honey syrup (2 parts honey : 1 part water by weight)

steps: Make 2:1 honey syrup by mixing two parts honey with one part warm water by weight; chill.
Sift matcha into a shaker and whisk with fresh lemon juice until smooth.
Add both whiskies, honey syrup, and a small pasteurized whole egg.
Dry shake without ice vigorously for 15–20 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for 12–15 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled stemmed cocktail glass.
Let foam settle for 20–30 seconds and dust lightly with sifted matcha.
alternatives: If smoke is overpowering, use 1½ oz / 45 mL Hibiki and ½ oz / 15 mL Ardbeg.
recipe.foodSafety: Use pasteurized egg; serve immediately; raw unpasteurized eggs carry Salmonella risk.

unresolvedQuestions: Test v1.0 at home and compare peat intensity, sweetness, acidity, and foam density to original.

recipes.notes: Version 1.0 experimental reconstruction based on strong smoke, balanced sweet-acid, rich texture, and no additional smoke presentation. Menu identifies ingredients but not proportions; all measured amounts are experimental, not the bar's verified formula.

recipes.name: E Hoo Pau Mai Tai
observations: Menu identifies El Dorado 8 and 12 Year rums, almond orgeat, honey, fig, coconut water, lime, absinthe and kiawe wood smoke.
Bartender sprayed absinthe onto the serving ice, then poured the cocktail from a smoke-filled container.
Bitters were applied to the top from a small dropper bottle after pouring; bitters are observed but not menu-listed.
Tasted dry and rum-forward; smoke was primarily an aroma on serving and near the top of the drink.

steps: Place serving ice in a rocks glass and mist with approximately two sprays of absinthe.
Shake rums, lime, orgeat, honey syrup, fig syrup and coconut water briefly with ice; strain into a separate pourable container.
Introduce a small amount of kiawe wood smoke into the container and cover for approximately 5–10 seconds, prioritizing aroma over heavy smoke infusion.
Pour over absinthe-sprayed ice and finish with 4–6 drops of aromatic bitters on the surface.
Optionally express orange peel over the glass; orange peel is an unconfirmed reconstruction detail.

unresolvedQuestions: Confirm actual honey, fig, and coconut-water proportions.
Identify bitters used in dropper bottle.
Test whether aroma and sweetness match the original.
recipes.notes: Experimental recipe reconstructed from menu and firsthand service notes. Original was rum-forward and dry; keep smoke aromatic rather than overpowering.

recipes.name: Shokudo's Aged Old Fashion
observations: Menu lists house-aged Toki whisky, Del Maguey Vida mezcal, orange bitters, Old Fashioned bitters and brown sugar.
Tasted smooth, whisky-forward and smoky; the drink was also smoked during presentation.

ingredients.name: Angostura aromatic bitters (substitute for unspecified Old Fashioned bitters)

steps: Add whisky, mezcal, brown sugar syrup and both bitters to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir until chilled and suitably diluted.
Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Express orange peel over the surface; use as garnish if desired.
Smoke the glass or finished cocktail with cherrywood or applewood for 15–30 seconds, then serve promptly.
recipe.glassware: Rocks glass with large ice cube

unresolvedQuestions: House-aging method and duration are unknown; this home version does not replicate aging.
Confirm the original bitters blend and smoke wood.
Test whether mezcal-to-whisky ratio matches the original.
recipes.notes: Reconstruction uses readily available ingredients and substitutes Angostura for unspecified Old Fashioned bitters. House-aged whisky is not replicated.
